description: Decoding one temporal field of a mutation payload. Positional arguments: the kind ("instant" or "dateOnly"), the raw value, and the field name. Epoch milliseconds is the ONLY accepted encoding — an ISO-8601 string is rejected even though it is what the same value looks like elsewhere on the wire, and a port that accepts both is wrong. Null and absent both decode to null, so a field cleared by the client and a field the client never sent are indistinguishable at this layer. A "dateOnly" value must land exactly on UTC midnight. Results are written here as ISO-8601 strings; an implementation converts its date type to ISO-8601 UTC before comparing.

cases.name: instant: an absent value is null
instant: the epoch itself is a value, not an absent field
instant: a sub-second epoch keeps its milliseconds
instant: an ISO-8601 string is rejected, not parsed
instant: a stringified epoch is rejected, not coerced
dateOnly: an absent value is null
dateOnly: the epoch itself is UTC midnight
dateOnly: one millisecond past midnight is rejected
dateOnly: a mid-day epoch is rejected
dateOnly: a YYYY-MM-DD string is rejected, not parsed
